Artemisinin-based combination therapies against artemether-lumefantrine: three direct comparisons, a network with no closed loop, and no indirect estimate

Among trials comparing an artemisinin-based combination therapy with artemether-lumefantrine, what is the PCR-corrected treatment failure in each direct comparison, and can the resulting network support an indirect comparison between the therapies that were never randomised against each other?

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: Report the three direct comparisons and compute NO indirect or mixed estimate, on a transitivity judgement rather than on the shape of the graph; and On the row whose treatment arm recorded no failures, store the boundary point estimate and NO interval, and add no constant to any cell

Cochrane Handbook sections: 11.2.1, 11.2.2, 11.4.4, 11.4.4.1, 10.4.4, 10.4.4.1

Section 11.2.1 defines the indirect comparison a common comparator makes available, so the path exists and the decision not to use it is a choice that must be argued. Section 11.2.2 supplies the argument: transitivity requires the sets of trials to be similar, on average, in all important factors other than the comparison being made, and here they differ in when the outcome was measured and in whether dosing was observed. Both are effect modifiers, which is what that section asks about. That each comparison rests on one study is not offered as a transitivity ground, because it is not one. Sections 11.4.4 and 11.4.4.1 are why the judgement cannot be checked: incoherence is measured in a closed loop as the difference between direct and indirect estimates, and this graph has none. Section 10.4.4.1 is the case of a study with no events in one or more arms. Section 10.4.4 records that software routines add a fixed value, typically one half, to all cells of a two-by-two table where the problem occurs, and that doing so 'usually has the undesirable effect of biasing study estimates towards no difference and over-estimating variances of study estimates'. The correction exists to let a study enter a pooled estimate. This row enters none, so the correction would buy an interval and no comparison, and it is not applied.

This is recorded as a declared departure under Cochrane Handbook §III.3.4.1: the review reports a pooled estimate for which no certainty assessment was made. Rating it here would require two assessors and an adjudicator, and a rating produced by neither is not a GRADE assessment whatever letter it carries. Of the five GRADE domains, 2 were assessed from this object: inconsistency -- not assessable -- no rating applied; publication bias -- not assessable -- no rating applied. 3 could not be: risk of bias, indirectness, imprecision. The specific inputs that would lift the refusal are explicit indirectness judgement for dp vs al; pooled.ci_high; pooled.ci_low; pooled.point; risk_of_bias. No overall certainty is issued from the remainder, because a GRADE level means all five domains were considered. CERTAINTY bound: Certainty lies between HIGH and VERY_LOW. The 2 domain(s) that were assessed give HIGH; the 3 unresolved domain(s) (risk_of_bias, indirectness, imprecision) could take it as low as VERY_LOW. This is a bound, not a rating: no letter is published, because choosing one inside the bound would be the judgement that has not been made. A bound is not a certainty rating and is not shown in the certainty column. It states what the assessed domains already establish and what the unassessed ones could still cost.

Interval absent reasonAn interval on this row would require adding a constant to each cell, and Cochrane Handbook section 10.4.4 warns that correction 'usually has the undesirable effect of biasing study estimates towards no difference'. Section 10.4.4.1 is the specific case, a study with no events in an arm. Nothing on this row is pooled with anything, so adding the constant would buy an interval and no comparison. The counts are what the trial reports and they are shown.

Summary

Question. Among trials comparing an artemisinin-based combination therapy with artemether-lumefantrine, what is the PCR-corrected treatment failure in each direct comparison, and can the resulting network support an indirect comparison between the therapies that were never randomised against each other?

What was found. 3 registered trials:

Table 19. Summary
RegistrationTrial
NCT01704508Guinea-Bissau, Bandim and Belem Health Centres
NCT04565184Cameroon, two secondary hospitals in Yaounde
NCT05192265Nigeria, Ibadan

What the trials found. No estimate below is combined with any other; each is the result of a single trial, reported as that trial reported it.

Table 20. Summary
TrialOutcomeResult
NCT04565184Artesunate-amodiaquine against artemether-lumefantrineRR 0.69 (95% CI 0.17 to 2.82)
NCT05192265Pyronaridine-artesunate against artemether-lumefantrineRR 0.21 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.98)

1 further per-trial estimate is recorded without a confidence interval and is not shown here, because a point estimate with no interval cannot be weighed.

Why no result is pooled. The trials identified do not report a shared, comparably measured outcome, so combining them would answer no single question.

What would change this. A pooled result becomes possible when trials reporting a shared, comparably measured outcome are available.

No pooled estimate, risk-of-bias assessment or certainty rating is published for this question, because there is no combined result for them to describe.

Not held in this object. No health-technology-assessment view is held in this object. That view needs an absolute effect at a baseline risk the reader chooses and a statement of which comparator the decision actually faces; neither is derivable from a pooled ratio alone, so nothing is generated here.
Not held in this object. No guideline view is held in this object. A GRADE evidence-to-decision framework needs values, resources, equity, acceptability and feasibility as well as the effects and the certainty, and a panel is better served by an empty cell it can see than by prose that reads as though it covered them.

This review can inform NONE of the twelve GRADE Evidence-to-Decision considerations. The full map is reproduced below so the gap is legible by row, and this panel is scored as carrying no content, because it carries none.

Page standard

UNSTAMPED — unknown-version. This page carries no build_stamp, so the standard it was built to cannot be established. That is a statement about the record, not a claim that the page is below standard.

Every number on this page is projected from a single canonical object, and each measured cell names the source analysis it was read from. That is what is machine-checked. It does not establish that the underlying sources are right, only that this page faithfully reports them.

OutcomePooled asWhich isTrials

What the trials themselves analysed could not be established from the records held, so this page does not claim that the pooled quantity matches the trials' own analysis. That is a gap in what we hold, not a statement that they agree.

Both intervals, and which one this page reports

dp_vs_al — not computed. Precision could be established for 0 of 1 contributing trials (missing: NCT01704508), and two are needed before an interval means anything.

asaq_vs_al — not computed. Precision could be established for 1 of 1 contributing trials, and two are needed before an interval means anything.

pa_vs_al — not computed. Precision could be established for 1 of 1 contributing trials, and two are needed before an interval means anything.

What has changed since these trials were last synthesised

No comparator is designated for this question, so this page does not state how current it is relative to one. Which published review answers the same question is a judgement, and this component refuses to make it by taking whichever identifier appears first — doing exactly that produced a search date from an adherence review of observational studies on an earlier run.

What the pooled effect means in people

dp_vs_al — not converted. The pooled measure is recorded as absent, which this component cannot place on a risk scale. An unrecognised measure is refused, not assumed to be a risk ratio.

asaq_vs_al — not converted. The pooled measure is recorded as absent, which this component cannot place on a risk scale. An unrecognised measure is refused, not assumed to be a risk ratio.

pa_vs_al — not converted. The pooled measure is recorded as absent, which this component cannot place on a risk scale. An unrecognised measure is refused, not assumed to be a risk ratio.

Safety, and every other outcome these trials reported

This object records no outcome besides the one pooled above. That is a statement about what has been extracted into this review, not about what the trials measured: a trial that reported harms this review has not extracted will look, from this page, exactly like a trial that reported none.

Which counts were used, and what difference it makes

This object records event counts from one source per trial and no alternative was sought, so this page cannot tell you whether the registry and the publication agree. ⚠️ That is not the same as saying they do. A registry posts counts as submitted and a publication reports them after endpoint adjudication; where those differ, the adjudicated figure is the trial's own final answer, and a review that never compared them cannot say which it is using.

What quantity this is, and what the trials actually analysed

This object does not record what quantity the contributing trials analysed, so this page cannot say whether the quantity it pools is theirs. ⚠️ That is an unchecked assumption, not a clean bill: a risk ratio over binary counts and a hazard ratio over person-time are different quantities, and a review that pools the first while the trials analysed the second will differ from them whenever follow-up differs between arms.

What a clinician or a programme should take from this

What this page cannot tell a clinician, and why. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for dp_vs_al. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for asaq_vs_al. direction — no pooled estimate with an interval for pa_vs_al. where it holds — no stratum reads as demonstrated. where it has not been shown — no stratum reads as not demonstrated. harms — no harm outcome is held at the trial-report tier. what it is not — no outcome is recorded as absent or not measurable. what it is conditional on — the object records no background care delivered alongside the intervention, so this page cannot say what its estimate is on top of. efficacy versus use — the object records no adherence finding.

6 classes we know about and cannot yet detect

Named because a taxonomy that lists only what it catches is marketing.

  • narrative-contradicts-its-own-table — prose that disagrees with the table beside it -- semantic, no instrument exists
  • value-does-not-reconcile-with-its-source — a stored number that does not follow from the document it cites; needs the source in hand, and we hold the primary report for a minority of trials
  • planned-field-shown-as-observed — a registered plan displayed in a field labelled as observation -- found by hand on this page's follow-up figure
  • prior-synthesis-value-presented-as-primary — a competitor's extraction reported as our own read; labelled here by hand, not detected
  • subgroup-claim-beyond-the-trial-strata — a subgroup statement the trial's own strata do not support
  • adjudicated-versus-submitted-counts — registry and publication disagreeing on event counts; detectable only where both are held
